questions.prompt: A photo app has 10 million daily active users. Each makes 20 API requests a day. What is the average request rate?
Traffic peaks in the evening at roughly 3× the average. Using your answer above, what peak rate should you plan for?
Each of those 10 million users views 50 photos a day, and a photo is 200 KB. What average outbound bandwidth does serving the photos take?
Each user posts 2 short comments a day, stored as 300 bytes each including metadata. Roughly how much new storage do comments need per year?
One API server comfortably handles 500 requests/s while keeping latency low. How many servers do you need for the 7,000 requests/s peak?
options: About 15, plus a spare or two

questions.prompt: Which of these takes the longest?
options: A network round trip within one data center
A random read from an SSD
A network round trip from California to Europe and back

questions.prompt: A catalog has 50 million items of 2 KB each. 20% of the items get 80% of the reads. About how much memory does a cache need to hold the popular items?
A service handles 100,000 reads/s and 1,000 writes/s, and its database is the bottleneck. What helps most?
options: Partitioning the database to spread out the writes
Adding a cache and read replicas to absorb the reads
Adding more indexes to speed up the writes
